newsitem.title: UK: Banks may be behind Anglo-Lonrho deal.
newsitem.headline: Banks may be behind Anglo-Lonrho deal.

text.p: Analysts said on Tuesday banks may have urged Lonrho's chief executive Dieter Bock to repay outstanding loans by exercising his put option and sell his 18.2 percent stake in the conglomerate to Anglo American.

Banks lent Bock the money to build up the stake in the 1990s. Bock in April agreed he could sell his holding to the South African mining powerhouse at 180 pence, while Anglo was given the option to buy at 220 pence.
"Bock put the shares to Anglo and that may indicate that his own banks said..."we want our loans repaid'," said analyst Charles Kernot at Paribas Capital Markets.
No-one at Lonrho was immediately available to comment.
Anglo said earlier that it had raised its stake in Lonrho to 25.9 percent after Bock had exercised his sell option.
The fact that the sell option rather than the call option was exercised should not be seen as a sign that Anglo was not keen on increasing its Lonrho holding, analysts said.

The main attraction for Anglo having a big Lonrho stake was considered the 30 percent stake the British conglomerate held in Ashanti Goldfields. Anglo said it would be constructive to work together with the Ashanti, but Ghana is believed to oppose any links with the South African company.
"Anglo has a very long game plan and I don't think that any of the comments coming out of Ghana are going to put them off," Kernot said.
"Anglo does have a very long time horizon, which is a quite a bit longer than any politician's," he added.

Lonrho said Bock would resign as chief executive but added he would remain interested in the conglomerate's trading operations. These businesses will be spun off after Lonrho has divested its hotels activities, eventually leaving the firm with only the mining sector eyed by Anglo. Lonrho said Bock remained interested in investing in the trading business.
The latest deal with Anglo has left Bock with ample supplies to buy a stake in the trading operations.
"When the unbundling has taken place Bock will be buying Anglo's 25.9 percent holding in Lonrho non-mining, non-hotels," Kernot predicted.
